title: US Court Lets Pannun Serve Summons on Doval, Ex-RAW Chief Through Delhi Courts
excerpt: A New York federal judge authorised service through three Delhi district courts under the Hague Convention. India rejected the lawsuit's allegations as fabricated and said service requests must go through its Law Ministry.
body:
• A US federal judge ruled on November 9 that Gurpatwant Singh Pannun may serve his civil lawsuit on National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former RAW chief Samant Goel through courts in Delhi.
  • Pannun must file a proposed service packet by November 30; the court clerk would then transmit the papers to the Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts.
  • India rejected the lawsuit's allegations as "fabricated and malicious" and said requests to serve judicial documents in India must go through the Ministry of Law and Justice.
  • The order decides only how the two men are formally notified of the case. It is not a ruling on the allegations, which India denies and which have not been established in court.

A United States federal court has allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to pursue serving summons on India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel through courts in Delhi, in his civil lawsuit alleging a 2023 conspiracy to assassinate him in New York. India rejected the allegations the following day, calling them fabricated and malicious, and said the route the court authorised is not the channel New Delhi recognises.

What the New York court allowed

US District Judge Katherine Polk Failla of the Southern District of New York granted Pannun's request on November 9 under Article 19 of the Hague Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents, which permits service by methods authorised under the domestic law of the country where the documents are to be delivered. The court relied on Section 29(c) of India's Code of Civil Procedure, read with a central government notification of January 12, 2009 extending that provision to Hague Convention countries, and on Order V Rule 21, which provides for transmitting summons to the court with jurisdiction over where a defendant resides, according to a detailed summary of the order by Desi Kaanoon.

Pannun identified three Delhi court complexes for service — Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari — based on jurisdiction over the two men's presumed residences. He must submit a proposed service packet by November 30, 2026, including the summonses, the proposed method of service and records of earlier attempts; the Clerk of Court would then transmit the documents to the Delhi courts.

Why service became the fight

Formal delivery of the papers has been contested for most of the case's life. Attempts to serve Doval personally during official visits to the United States were blocked by security personnel, and in April 2025 the court found the complaint had not been delivered to him during a visit to Washington that February. On April 1, 2026, the court also rejected service by email, by publication, and through diplomatic channels under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, citing India's reservation to Article 8 of the Hague Convention.

Service on the Government of India itself was handled separately: the US State Department transmitted that summons through diplomatic channels, via a note signed on September 30 and handed over on October 9, according to reporting on the order.

The lawsuit, and India's response

Pannun, general counsel of Sikhs for Justice, filed the suit in 2024 — case number 24 Civ. 7021 — naming the Government of India, Doval, Goel, Vikram Yadav, Nikhil Gupta and 50 unnamed defendants. He alleges they conspired to assassinate him at his New York residence in retaliation for his role in the movement seeking an independent Sikh state. The allegations have not been established in court.

"We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials."

— Randhir Jaiswal, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson

Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal dismissed the allegations at a media briefing and described the litigation as frivolous, Channel 24 India reported. He said requests to serve judicial documents in India must be routed through the Ministry of Law and Justice, which is India's designated central authority under the Hague Convention — the standard route the court's order works around rather than through.

Separate from the criminal case

The civil suit is distinct from the US criminal prosecution arising from the alleged 2023 plot. In that case, the US Justice Department announced in February 2026 that Indian national Nikhil Gupta had pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. Monday's order was issued only in Pannun's civil suit, and concerns only the process of notifying two of its defendants.

What happens next

The immediate deadline is November 30, when Pannun's service packet is due. If the court approves it, the papers travel to the three Delhi courts for delivery. Whether India cooperates, objects, or insists on the Law Ministry channel will decide whether the two-year-old lawsuit can move from notification to substance.
